Hi Ravi — thanks for the quick context and the logs. We can potentially approve a temporary alignment but need to lock a few guardrails first so the change doesn't create at-least-once semantics for your downstream consumers. A couple quick clarifying questions:

1) How are you currently submitting jobs (API endpoint /jobs/submit, and do you attach X-Request-Id or job_id)?
2) Rough weekly volume (number of rows per night and number of concurrent jobs)?
3) Any SLA credit or termination concerns from procurement/legal on your side if the carveout is granted?

Proposed interim approach from our side:
- Require an idempotency token on submission (X-Idempotency-Key or job_id).
- Server-side dedupe keys retained for 72h; clients should still send tokens and tolerate retry responses.
- Limit retries to a capped backoff (3 attempts recommended) and require a safe-retry flag for large jobs.

I'll route this internally for approval and return with the formal exception doc / next steps.

Best,

Karthik / Laura — forwarding ACME's request. Key points: nightly bulk jobs growing to 3–5h, asking for 6-hour completion window for nights starting 01:00 PST, asking for guidance on retries/idempotency. Attached are logs and their filled exception form.

My recommended mitigation to approve a temporary carveout (90 days) if we require the following from ACME before we sign:
- Idempotency token (X-Idempotency-Key) required for each job submission; job API must return a 409 if duplicate is detected within dedupe TTL.
- Server will retain dedupe keys for 72 hours; clients must provide a job footprint (row counts + input checksum).
- Retries: capped at 3 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter; jobs must set safe-retry flag for deferred retries.
- Instrumentation/telemetry: ACME must enable per-job tracing and include a correlation_id so our console can show job-level status and retries.
- Compensation: offer a one-time usage credit (10% of the month's nightly inference bill) if jobs repeatedly miss the carved window beyond the 90-day review.

Questions for you:
- Karthik: Are the 72h dedupe TTL and 3 retry cap operationally sufficient for our runtime internals? Any additional kernel/runtime-level constraints?
- Laura: Do we approve a 90-day temporary carveout with the proposed credit slab, and should legal add explicit termination language?

Thanks — I can prep the exception form for signature once we align.

Regards,
Marissa

--- Message 4 (technical reply) ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:21:10 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Request for extended completion window on nightly bulk jobs / ACME (please advise)

Marissa — technical notes and constraints:
- 72h dedupe TTL is fine from the runtime perspective; we already have KV store sharding that supports this retention for dedupe keys. 48–72h is the sweet spot to balance disk / memory retention vs client convenience.
- Require X-Idempotency-Key (UUID) or job_id pair (client-generated) — we should add validation in the SDKs to encourage this.
- Retries: recommend 3 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 10s, doubling, and adding 30–60s jitter for long tail jobs. After third failure, job should surface a terminal error and downstream can re-submit as a new job with a new idempotency key.
- For very large jobs (>1M rows) suggest we also require a sequence_id per chunk and allow chunk-level retries. That avoids reprocessing completed chunks and preserves near-exact-once semantics.
- If we grant a window extension, add a soft-fallback policy: after N seconds from scheduled end, automatically switch to a lower-throughput but higher-stability model variant to finish remaining items within the extended window. This reduces credits paid and preserves customer experience.

Operational ask: we should flag this as a time-limited carveout and add a telemetry alert (INF-7923) that triggers if more than 2% of nightly jobs exceed the carved window. Once the metric stabilizes for 30 days, we re-evaluate.

Karthik

Redwood Inference

- Carveout window: nightly jobs starting 01:00 PST may have up to 6 hours to complete (01:00 — 07:00 PST).
- Duration: 90 days (01 Dec 2027 — 01 Mar 2028) pending telemetry review.

- Retries: max 3 attempts, exponential backoff + jitter. For jobs >1M rows, submit chunked sequence_ids so only incomplete chunks are retried.
- Fallback: we will enable automatic fallback to a lower-throughput model variant if the job is at risk of missing the carved end time.
- Compensation: 10% one-time usage credit as described if the carved window is missed repeatedly per the thresholds above.

Next steps:
1) Please review, sign the attached SLA-exception form and return via DocuSign: https://docusign.redwood.com/ACME-SLA-EX-504

3) We'll enable telemetry and create INF-7923 and link it to your account so you can see per-job status in the console.

Attached: signed exception form (pending signature) and a short implementation checklist for your engineers.
